heading: Bank Liability for Scam Transfers: A Consumer Commission View
tldr: A recent Consumer Commission ruling held a bank liable even when a customer voluntarily transferred funds to a scammer.
The commission found the bank negligent for not acting on suspicious transaction patterns, despite OTP authorisations.
This ruling challenges the traditional view that OTP-verified transactions automatically absolve banks of responsibility.
It underscores the bank's duty of care to monitor for unusual activity and protect customer interests.
Customers who fall victim to scams after voluntarily transferring money may still have recourse if bank negligence can be proven.
caption:
Ever wondered if your bank is responsible if you get scammed, even if you approve the transfer? A new ruling says banks might be. Even with OTPs, banks have a duty to spot strange activity and protect your money. This could mean more safety for us all. Read the full article to understand how this might affect you.
